generations.name: bZ4X launch
generations.notes: Launch as bZ4X: FWD 71.4 kWh (DC up to 150 kW); AWD 72.8 kWh CATL pack (DC up to 100 kW, about an hour to 80%). Same in CA and US. Confidence: high (researched 2026-11-19, owner review pending). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota_bZ4X ; https://insideevs.com/news/585939/toyota-bz4x-awd-fast-charging-curve/

generations.name: bZ4X 2024 charging update
generations.notes: Same packs. A battery thermal upgrade (water-to-water heat exchanger, heating valve) speeds up cold-weather DC charging; reviews report the AWD peak raised from 100 to 150 kW. Toyota's US release describes the thermal hardware but gives no new peak kW; the 150 kW AWD figure comes from reviews. Carscoops initially reported the US might not get the change. Keep this split only if 2024-2025 curves really differ from 2023. Confidence: low (researched 2026-11-19, owner review pending). Sources: https://guideautoweb.com/en/articles/73202/2024-toyota-bz4x-loses-base-model-improves-cold-weather-charging ; https://evpulse.com/reviews/2024-toyota-bz4x-awd-limited-review-significantly-improved-still-hard-to-recommend

generations.name: 2026 refresh (bZ)
generations.notes: Renamed bZ. New packs: 57.7 kWh LFP (XLE FWD) and 74.7 kWh (US figure; Toyota Canada quotes 77 kWh total); DC up to 150 kW, 10-80% in about 30 min; native NACS; 11 kW AC. Same name and year in CA and US. 74.7 (US) vs 77 kWh (CA) is probably usable vs total for one pack. The bZ Woodland (2026 US / 2027 CA on sale) is a separate wagon model, not part of this line. Confidence: high (researched 2026-11-19, owner review pending). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota_bZ4X ; https://media.toyota.ca/en/releases/2025/toyota-bz-all-electric-suv-adds-range--charging-and-exterior-upd.html
